title: Chapter 172: The Monster Behind the Door
html:
Such a meteoric rise in popularity exceeded every expectation.

I warned Qin Guang, and he refused to listen, so this isn’t my fault. Fortunately, Mu Yang High School isn’t especially dangerous, and its ghosts aren’t malicious. He should survive.Chen Ge still considered himself kind.I hope he recovers quickly and thinks twice before stealing anyone else’s work.

He seized the opportunity to promote his attraction. Countless viewers would remember Western Jiujiang’s House of Horrors after tonight. Popularity multiplied like rising dough; for the foreseeable future, visitors should arrive in a steady stream.

“We need to discuss a new contract. I also have a question.” Still under enormous pressure himself, Liu Dao remained on the line. “You arranged this entire broadcast, correct? Your Haunted House team controls the location and performances?”

Partnership had not taught Liu Dao much about Chen Ge. He knew only that a Haunted House owner might employ professional actors and design convincing scares. As someone who rejected the supernatural, he instinctively sought a logical explanation for everything he saw.

“More or less.” Chen Ge answered vaguely. He did have a team at the Haunted House, but aside from Xu Wan, none of its members could be revealed.

“I knew you weren’t alone in there.” Liu Dao sighed. “Your wrist camera fell during the fight. After you ran out, it began moving across the floor. Sister Lee almost believed a real ghost had appeared.”

“What?” Chen Ge glanced at his wrist. The camera was gone, probably knocked loose during the struggle.

“Look, it’s moving again!”

He hid the chat and checked the smaller feed in the corner. The wrist camera was advancing through the corridor, apparently caught on the nurse’s uniform—and coming straight toward him.

“She survived all that? Is the hospital restoring her?”

Unaware of the danger, Liu Dao offered earnest advice. “Contact your actor and tell him to stay off-camera. That will build anticipation.”

“Anticipation?” Chen Ge ended the call and sprinted upstairs. The livestream now showed one camera fleeing from the other.

The dual perspective was new to both audience and host. In the third-floor corridor, Chen Ge glanced at his phone—and saw his own back.

“She has caught up to me!”

Unable to destroy her permanently, he plunged into the stairwell, doubled back to the second floor, shook her pursuit, and raced down to the first.

The nurse pursued by instinct alone. Once she lost him, she resumed searching each room in turn.

Unlike a mirror monster, the nurse has no independent will. She has almost merged with the hospital itself.

After she moved away, Chen Ge emerged. Everything had begun on this level. The stench is even stronger here.

The first-floor corridor looked unlike every other. Wormlike shapes squirmed in cracks beneath his feet. Faded red blotches bruised the walls, and when he peeled away the surface, he found the color had soaked deep into the plaster, like blood beneath living skin.

“The director’s letters mentioned something similar, but he said that the weird changes were limited to the walls adjacent to Room 3.”

Ten rooms lined the floor, corresponding to ten patients. The nearest, Room 10, had a steel door more suited to a prison cell than a hospital. Nothing Chen Ge tried could move it.

“The quality is good. Even after so many years, there are no signs of it getting loose.”

Room 10 had housed the patient called the Devil. Doctor Gao believed his illness had probably killed him, but exceptions always existed.

Several former patients had already returned tonight. Patient Number 10 might still live among them.

Steel also sealed Rooms 8 and 9. Opening either would create too much noise. This was no time for sightseeing; Chen Ge hurried toward Room 3.

The walls peeled around him as bloodlike fluid seeped from within. Dolls protruded beneath the mattresses, poised as though ready to seize his ankles.

Bruise-colored patches filled every corner. When he touched one, lines resembling blood vessels spread beneath his hand. The building itself appeared to bleed.

The stench grew painfully pungent. Fighting nausea, he approached Room 3 until its door emerged from the gloom.

Blood had dyed it entirely red. It stood half-open, a NO ENTRY sign hanging from the handle.

“The door that destroyed this hospital.”

Only now did the full danger of his situation register. He forced his legs forward, though neither hammer nor cleaver offered reassurance. Every cell screamed at him to flee, while a quiet voice deep in his mind urged him closer.

Hair standing across his body, he stopped before Room 3. Amid blood-soaked walls, the silent door resembled the Third Sick Hall’s heart, with everything else built around it.

Will this happen to the door in my Haunted House if I leave it be?

Through the gap, he saw a red ceiling, red walls, a red bed—an entire room stained crimson. The threshold divided two utterly different worlds.

He reached for the door, intending to close it. The instant it moved, a familiar sound reached him.

He had heard it at the Haunted House: something heavy dragging across the floor.
